title: Chocolate Sandwich Cookies with Vanilla Cream
summary: Crisp chocolate wafer biscuits sandwiched with a smooth vanilla buttercream filling.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Beat the wet ingredients
steps.text: Beat the softened butter, caster sugar, golden syrup, salt and vanilla together for 2 minutes, until creamy and well combined. The golden syrup adds moisture and a touch of chew to what would otherwise be a very dry, cocoa-heavy dough. No need to worry about overbeating here, since there's no egg to toughen.

steps.title: Bring in the dry ingredients
steps.text: Add the cocoa, flour and bicarbonate of soda and mix on low speed until the dough looks crumbly at first, then comes together into a stiff, cohesive mass. Only add the milk if the dough genuinely won't hold together, a teaspoon at a time. With no egg in the recipe, this dough bakes up crisp and snappy rather than soft.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Shape the dough into two flat discs, wrap them, and chill for 30-60 minutes. Chilling makes the dough firm enough to roll thinly without tearing or sticking. This rest also lets the cocoa's flavour settle through the dough.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) for at least 20 minutes, with a shelf in the middle. The relatively gentle temperature helps the thin wafers dry out evenly without the edges scorching before the centres set. Line two large metal trays with baking paper ready for the cut rounds.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll the dough between sheets of baking paper to about 3 mm thick, then cut into rounds with a 5 cm cutter. Re-roll the scraps once to use up the dough, and space the rounds 2 cm apart on the lined trays. Rolling between paper keeps this sticky, cocoa-dark dough from picking up extra flour, which can dry the wafers out.

steps.title: Bake the wafers
steps.text: Bake for 13-15 minutes, until the wafers feel dry and firm at the edges and look slightly darker right at the rim. Because the dough is already dark with cocoa, colour alone is hard to read here, so trust the firm edge as your main cue. The centres will still feel a touch soft when they come out, but that firms up as they cool.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Leave the wafers on the tray for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool fully and go properly crisp. Don't try to sandwich them while they're still warm, as the filling will simply melt and slide off. They need to be completely cold and crisp before filling.

steps.title: Make the vanilla cream
steps.text: Beat the soft butter, icing sugar, vanilla and salt together for 3 minutes until stiff and smooth, adding milk a few drops at a time if needed to loosen it. Beating this long whips enough air into the filling to keep it light rather than dense and greasy. The finished cream should hold its shape on a spoon.

steps.title: Fill and rest
steps.text: Pipe or spoon a heaped teaspoon of the vanilla cream onto the flat side of half the wafers, then top with the remaining wafers and press together gently. Rest the sandwiches for 30 minutes to let the filling firm up before serving. Makes about 22 sandwiches.

tips: Roll the dough between baking paper rather than on a floured surface — extra flour worked into this dark dough can dry the wafers out and dull the chocolate flavour.
Judge doneness by the firm edge, not colour; a common mistake is underbaking dark cocoa dough because it already looks done.
Make sure the wafers are completely cold before filling, or the warmth will melt the buttercream straight out of the sandwich.
Only add milk to the dough or filling a little at a time — both can turn from stiff to runny with just an extra splash.
Re-roll scraps only once; dough rolled a third time toughens and the wafers lose their snap.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store filled sandwiches in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days, or chill for up to a week if the room is warm. Unfilled wafers freeze for up to 2 months; thaw and fill fresh.
